title: Changing, Adding and Removing Python List Items
learningObjectives: Explain the behavior of changing, adding and removing python list items.
Select appropriate list operations for a given task.
Predict the effect of indexing, mutation and copying.
Write readable code that processes list data.
Avoid common list-related errors and side effects.

understand.concept: Lists are mutable, so an item can be changed by assigning to an index. append adds one item to the end; insert adds an item at a specified position; extend adds items from an iterable. remove deletes the first matching value, pop removes and returns an item, and del or clear can remove items in other ways.
understand.whyItMatters: List mutation supports tasks such as updating shopping carts, editing queues and maintaining changing records.
understand.analogy: A list is like an editable sequence of cards: replace a card, add new cards or remove selected cards.
understand.analogyLimit: Mutating a list changes the existing object. Other variables referring to the same list can observe the changes.

explain.narrative:
## 1. Change an item

Assign a new value to a valid index, such as `items[1] = 'new'`.

## 2. Add items

Use append for one item, insert for a position, and extend for items from another iterable.

## 3. Remove items

Use remove for a matching value, pop for an index (or the last item), del for an index or slice, and clear to empty the list.

## 4. Choose the right operation

append adds its argument as one item; extend iterates over the supplied iterable.

examples.title: Change an item
examples.explanation: Assignment at index one replaces the existing value.

examples.title: Append one item
examples.explanation: append adds its argument as one new item at the end.

examples.title: Extend with multiple items
examples.explanation: extend adds each item from the iterable.

examples.title: Insert and remove a value
examples.explanation: insert places an item at index one and remove deletes the first matching c.

examples.title: Pop returns a removed item
examples.explanation: pop without an index removes and returns the last item.

practise.guidedTask: Start with a list of three tasks. Append one task, insert one at the beginning, change an item and remove one value.
practise.independentTask: Model a small shopping list. Demonstrate append, extend, insert, remove, pop and clear, explaining how each changes the original list.
hints: Assign to an index to replace an item.
extend adds items from an iterable.
remove deletes the first matching value.
pop removes and returns an item.
practise.challenge: Compare append([3, 4]) with extend([3, 4]) and predict the different resulting list structures.

questions.prompt: Which method adds one item to the end?
questions.explanation: append adds its argument as a single item.

questions.prompt: Which method adds each item from an iterable?
questions.explanation: extend iterates over the supplied iterable and adds its elements.

questions.prompt: What does pop() return when called without an index?
options: The first item without removing it
questions.explanation: pop removes and returns the last item by default.
remove deletes the first occurrence of the specified value.

options: Removes all items from the list
questions.answer: Removes all items from the list
questions.explanation: clear empties the existing list object.
